newsitem.title: INDIA: India court overturns Uttar Pradesh federal rule.
newsitem.headline: India court overturns Uttar Pradesh federal rule.

text.p: India's opposition Hindu nationalists demanded on Thursday that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda resign after a court ordered the lifting of federal rule in India's most populous state.

Court officials in the capital of Uttar Pradesh state, Lucknow, said the Allahabad High Court upheld an appeal by leaders of the main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) against federal rule.

"We have won in court and we want justice," BJP leader Atal Behari Vajpayee was quoted by the Press Trust of India (PTI) as saying. "We demand the resignation of the United Front government as it has murdered democracy."

President Shankar Dayal Sharma, bowing to a decision by Deve Gowda's cabinet, in October imposed direct rule on the northern state after local elections threw up a hung assembly and efforts to form a government failed.
The BJP, which emerged from the polls as the largest single party in the state legislature, had appealed to the court, arguing they had been denied a chance to form a government.
"Our stand has been upheld. We have already said the manner in which it was done was unconstitutional," BJP lawyer R.N. Trivedi told Reuters in the state capital Lucknow.
The court gave the federal government until December 25 to challenge the order. If no appeal were lodged, renewed efforts to form a state government would get underway.

The BJP won 177 seats in the 425-member assembly, followed by Deve Gowda's United Front coalition with 134 seats. The low caste Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) won 67 seats and its ally, the Congress party, took 33 seats.

The assembly was suspended but not dissolved after imposition of president's rule in the politically crucial state, which sends 85 lawmakers to the 545-member federal parliament, more than any other of India's 26 states.
The decision to impose federal rule over Uttar Pradesh, which has 140 million people, provoked an uproar from the BJP, which had expected an invitation to form the government.
The BJP briefly held power in the state from 1991. But New Delhi dismissed its government after Hindu zealots demolished a 16th century mosque in Ayodhya town in December 1992.
